after.title: How Much Does FCA Authorisation Cost for a Car Dealer?
after.seoTitle: FCA Authorisation Cost for Car Dealers | 009 Compliance
after.description: What a consumer credit licence costs now: the FCA application fee, annual FCA fees and levies, and other costs car dealers should plan for before applying.
after.answer: For a car dealer applying for limited permission, the FCA application fee is £560 (Category 2), paid in Connect when you submit. It is not refunded if the application is withdrawn or refused. Once authorised, you pay an annual FCA fee, with a minimum fee for limited-permission firms, plus levies the FCA collects for other bodies. There is no separate consumer credit licence fee: the licence is now FCA authorisation.

sections.title: What a consumer credit licence costs now
paragraphs: The FCA took over consumer credit regulation from the Office of Fair Trading on 1 April 2014. A search for a “consumer credit licence cost” or an “FCA licence price” is now a question about the cost of FCA authorisation.

The FCA’s charges come in two parts: a one-off application fee, then annual fees and levies once the firm is authorised. The cost of preparing the application, including any outside help, is separate from FCA fees.

sections.title: The FCA application fee
paragraphs: The fee pays for the FCA’s assessment, not for an approval.
rows: Limited permission (fee-block CC1)
Category 2 application fee: £560.
Range across all applications
From £280 (Category 1) up to £225,170 (Category 10).
When it is paid
In Connect, by credit or debit card. You have to pay the fee to submit the application.
Refunds

The FCA’s fees page says the fee is non-refundable. If the FCA rejects a submission without assessing it because minimum information is missing, you can resubmit it with the missing information. Check the FCA’s current fees page on refunds.

sections.title: Annual FCA fees and levies
paragraphs: The FCA says 2026/27 is the final year of its phased increases to consumer credit minimum fees, with future increases linked to inflation.
columns: What applies to a limited-permission firm
rows: Annual FCA fee
Fee-block CC01 (credit-related regulated activities with limited permission), based on consumer credit annual income, subject to a minimum fee.
Minimum fee for 2026/27
£1,100, the same for every consumer credit related income band (up to £10,000, £10,000 to £100,000 and over £100,000). In earlier fee years the bands had different minimums.
Consumer credit income
For credit broking, commission and related income. Where there is no commission income, the FCA’s proxy is 5% of the value of the credit agreement.
Invoices
Issued from July each year and usually due 30 days from the invoice date.
Levies collected by the FCA
All firms pay the Financial Guidance levy, limited-permission (CC1) firms pay a flat illegal money lending levy, and the Financial Ombudsman Service levy may apply. The amounts are set each year.

after.title: How to Apply for FCA Limited Permission as a Car Dealer
after.seoTitle: How to Apply for FCA Limited Permission as a Car Dealer
after.description: Step by step: how car dealers apply for FCA limited permission, from Connect set-up and application sections to paying the fee and answering FCA questions.
after.answer: To apply for FCA limited permission, confirm the activities and the legal entity, register for the FCA’s Connect system, choose limited permission, complete the application form and the forms for the people involved, attach your business plan, forecasts and supporting material, pay the application fee and submit. Do not start regulated activity until the FCA has authorised the firm.

sections.title: Step 1: confirm the permission and the applicant
paragraphs: The FCA’s motor-dealer guidance says a dealer that owns the vehicles it sells meets its definition of a supplier and can apply for limited permission. Introducing customers to finance for purposes other than buying or leasing the vehicles you sell needs full permission.
Decide which legal entity will hold the permission before you start the forms. The application, website and customer process should all describe the same business.

sources.label: FCA: permissions and applications for motor dealers

sections.title: Step 2: register for Connect and start the application
paragraphs: Applications are made on the FCA’s Connect system. An unauthorised firm registers for Standard Connect, which covers new authorisation applications, and selects limited or full permission when it starts the application.
The FCA asks applicants to read its credit broker guidance in full before submitting through Connect.

sections.title: Step 5: after you submit
paragraphs: A case officer is assigned and you can track progress in Connect. The FCA usually has questions, so respond by the dates it gives. Substantive changes after submission may lead the FCA to ask you to withdraw and reapply.

By law the FCA must decide a complete application within 6 months and an incomplete one within 12 months. Your firm must not carry on regulated activities while the application is under review unless an exemption or temporary permission applies.

after.title: FCA Application Refused or Rejected: What Motor Dealers Can Do
after.seoTitle: FCA Application Refused? Options for Motor Dealers
after.description: Why the FCA refuses or rejects applications, how this differs from withdrawal, what a warning notice means and what to change before you reapply.
after.answer: An FCA refusal follows a set process: the FCA gives feedback and you can withdraw; if you continue, you receive a warning notice and can make written representations before any decision notice, which you can refer to the Upper Tribunal. A submission rejected for missing minimum information is different: you can resubmit it with the missing information. Check the FCA’s current fees page on refunds.

sections.title: Rejected, withdrawn or refused: the difference
rows: Rejected
The FCA rejects a submission without assessing it if minimum information is missing and explains why.
Resubmit with the missing information. Check the FCA’s current fees page on refunds.
Withdrawn
The applicant can withdraw at any time before the application is determined. The fee is not refunded.
Another application can be made later.
Refused
The FCA recommends refusal where it thinks the application does not meet the standard for authorisation. The fee is not refunded.
The warning notice and decision notice process applies.

sections.title: Why applications fall short
paragraphs: The FCA assesses applicants against the threshold conditions, which include effective supervision and appropriate resources. Its review of applications gives examples of weaknesses, such as relying on a compliance consultant without being able to show the firm understands its own obligations, and not submitting historic financial accounts with the initial application.
The FCA also says a business model should not be generic, and that it might refuse an application if information is deliberately withheld, false or incomplete.

sections.title: Warning notice, representations and decision notice
paragraphs: The deadline for referring a decision notice to the Upper Tribunal is confirmed in the notice itself.
bullets: Before a warning notice, the FCA gives feedback. If you withdraw at this stage, the assessment ends.
A warning notice sets out the proposed refusal and the reasons, and allows at least 14 days for representations. The FCA can extend the period.
Representations are normally made in writing to the FCA’s decision maker, who can still decide not to refuse.
A decision notice states any right to refer the matter to the Upper Tribunal and the procedure. Once it is given, the application has been determined and cannot be withdrawn.
If the decision notice is not referred, the FCA issues a final notice. The FCA may publish decision and final notices.

faqs.question: Is the application fee refunded if the FCA refuses my application?
faqs.answer: No. The FCA says the application fee is non-refundable, including after a refusal or a withdrawal. A submission rejected for missing minimum information can be resubmitted with that information; check the FCA’s current fees page on refunds.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw instead of being refused?
faqs.answer: Yes, at any time before the application is determined, including after informal feedback. Once a decision notice is given, the application has been determined and cannot be withdrawn.

faqs.question: How long do I have to respond to a warning notice?
faqs.answer: The warning notice sets the period, which must be at least 14 days. The FCA can extend it.

faqs.question: Can I challenge a refusal?
faqs.answer: Yes. An applicant can refer the decision to the Upper Tribunal. The decision notice confirms the right, the procedure and the deadline.

after.title: How to Offer PCP and HP Car Finance to Your Customers
after.seoTitle: How to Offer Car Finance (PCP and HP) as a Dealer
after.description: How dealers start offering PCP and HP finance: FCA authorisation, joining lender panels, and the FCA rules on promotions, commission and customers.
after.answer: To offer PCP and HP finance, a dealer first needs FCA permission for credit broking or an appointed representative arrangement, then arrangements with the lenders or brokers it will introduce customers to. Once live, FCA rules apply: promotions must say you are a credit broker, not a lender, commission must be disclosed where it could affect your impartiality or the customer’s decision, and the Consumer Duty applies.

sections.title: What you are offering: PCP and HP
paragraphs: Under a hire-purchase agreement the customer hires the vehicle and ownership passes once the terms are met. The FCA’s car finance guidance treats personal contract purchase (PCP) as a type of hire-purchase agreement. When a dealer introduces a customer to a lender for either, it is carrying on credit broking.
Check each product’s actual terms; the lender is the party that provides the credit.

sources.label: legislation.gov.uk: Consumer Credit Act 1974 s.189 — definitions
FCA: car finance complaints and PCP/HP agreements
legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 36A — credit broking

sections.title: Step 1: get the right permission
paragraphs: A dealer that owns its stock and introduces customers to third-party finance is likely to need limited permission for secondary credit broking. Part-exchanges with outstanding finance also need debt adjusting and debt counselling permissions. The alternative is an appointed representative arrangement with an authorised principal.

sources.label: FCA: permissions and applications for motor dealers

sections.title: Step 2: set up lender and broker arrangements
paragraphs: The FCA expects your regulatory business plan to identify the lenders or brokers you intend to work with and to state any fees you charge and what commission you will earn. Agree with each one how introductions, documents and complaints will be handled, and record the commission terms you will need to disclose.
Ask each lender or broker what it requires before it accepts introductions from your dealership.

sources.label: FCA: permissions and applications for motor dealers

sections.title: Step 3: the rules once you offer finance
columns: What it means for a dealer
rows: Broker, not lender (CONC 3.7.7R)
Financial promotions must state prominently that you are a credit broker and not a lender.
Legal name (CONC 3.7.5R)
Promotions and customer communications must show your legal name as it appears on the Financial Services Register, not only a trading name.
Extent of powers (CONC 3.7.3R)
Say whether you work exclusively with one or more lenders or independently.
Representative example (CONC 3.5)
Where CONC 3.5 requires one, a finance promotion must include a representative example with the specified information.
Commission disclosure (CONC 4.5.3R)
Disclose the existence and nature of commission prominently and in good time where it could affect your impartiality or the customer’s decision, and how it may affect what the customer pays.
No discretionary commission (CONC 4.5.6R)
Since 28 January 2021, lenders and brokers must not use discretionary commission arrangements in motor finance.
Consumer Duty
The FCA says the Consumer Duty requires your firm to put its customers’ needs first.

sections.title: Fictional example: a first finance customer
paragraphs: Fictional example. Example Motor Sales Ltd has limited permission and an arrangement with a lender. A customer asks about PCP on a used car. The salesperson explains that the dealership is a credit broker, not a lender, discloses the commission arrangement and how it can affect the cost, and gives the lender’s representative example.
The dealer passes the application to the lender, which makes the lending decision, and keeps a record of what the customer was told.

faqs.question: Do I need FCA authorisation to offer PCP finance?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most cases. Introducing customers to PCP or HP finance is credit broking, which needs FCA permission or an appointed representative arrangement.

faqs.question: What are the FCA rules for offering car finance as a dealer?
faqs.answer: The main rules are in CONC: promotions must say you are a broker, not a lender, and show your legal name; commission must be disclosed where it could affect your impartiality or the customer’s decision; and discretionary commission arrangements are banned. The Consumer Duty also applies.

faqs.question: Do I have to tell customers how much commission I earn?
faqs.answer: You must disclose the existence and nature of commission where CONC 4.5.3R applies, and the amount, or likely amount, if the customer asks.

faqs.question: Can I set the customer’s interest rate to earn more commission?
faqs.answer: No. Discretionary commission arrangements, which let a broker adjust the rate and earn more commission, have been banned in motor finance since 28 January 2021.

after.title: What Is CCR007?
after.seoTitle: What Is CCR007? FCA Key Data Return | 009 Compliance
after.description: CCR007 is the FCA Key Data return for limited-permission credit firms: who submits it, how often, what it asks and how it links to CCR009.
after.answer: CCR007 is the FCA’s Key Data return for credit firms with limited permission, and all firms with limited permission must submit it. It asks for revenue, transaction and complaint figures for credit-related regulated activities, reported on a calendar-year basis from 2026. Dealers that also submit CCR009 can enter zero in some CCR007 fields.

sections.title: What CCR007 is and who submits it
paragraphs: CCR007 is the data item “Key Data for Credit Firms with Limited Permissions”. The FCA says all firms with limited permission must submit it, so a car dealer with limited permission for secondary credit broking should expect it on its reporting schedule.
Consumer credit returns are submitted through RegData, the FCA’s online data collection platform. Check your firm’s schedule there for the returns and due dates that apply.

sources.label: FCA: consumer credit reporting
FCA: completing CCR007

sections.title: What it asks for
paragraphs: The last item is the income figure the FCA uses to calculate annual fees.
bullets: Revenue from credit-related regulated activities.
Total revenue, including from other activities.
Number of transactions involving credit-related regulated activities in the period.
Number of complaints about credit-related regulated activities received in the period.
The credit-related regulated activity that generated the most turnover.
Total annual income as defined for FCA fees (FEES 4 Annex 11BR).

sources.label: FCA: completing CCR007
FCA: consumer credit income for fees

sections.title: When it is due
paragraphs: From 2026, the FCA requires CCR007 and CCR009 to be reported on a calendar-year basis, 1 January to 31 December, rather than by reference to the firm’s accounting reference date. The FCA’s reporting table gives 30 business days to submit CCR007, compared with 40 for CCR009.
The FCA says firms that do not complete their reporting by the due date are subject to an administrative fee of £100.

sources.label: FCA: consumer credit reporting
FCA Handbook: SUP 16.12 — reporting schedules
FCA: completing CCR007

sections.title: How CCR009 changed CCR007
paragraphs: CCR009 came into effect on 7 May 2025. Firms submitting CCR009 may report zero in CCR007 fields 1A and 3A where those fields relate only to credit broking or not-for-profit debt management. Accurate figures are still needed for other limited-permission activities and in all the remaining fields.

sources.label: FCA: CCR009 reporting, scope and submission

sections.title: Fictional example: one dealer, two returns
paragraphs: Fictional example. Example Motors Ltd has limited permission for secondary credit broking. Its schedule shows CCR007 and CCR009 for the 2026 calendar year. It gathers its commission income, the number of transactions and the complaints received for the year.
Because fields 1A and 3A relate only to its credit broking, it enters zero there, completes the remaining CCR007 fields accurately and answers the CCR009 questions separately.

sources.label: FCA: CCR009 reporting, scope and submission

faqs.question: Who has to submit CCR007?
faqs.answer: The FCA says all firms with limited permission must submit CCR007. Check your firm’s reporting schedule in RegData.

faqs.question: Is CCR007 the same as CCR009?
faqs.answer: No. CCR007 is the Key Data return for limited-permission firms; CCR009 covers relevant ancillary credit firms. A limited-permission dealer can need to submit both.

faqs.question: What period does CCR007 cover?
faqs.answer: From 2026, the calendar year from 1 January to 31 December, not the firm’s accounting reference date.

after.title: Do Van and Commercial Vehicle Dealers Need FCA Permission?
after.seoTitle: FCA Permissions for Van and Commercial Vehicle Dealers
after.description: Selling vans to sole traders or small partnerships? Some business vehicle finance is still regulated consumer credit. See which customers are covered.
after.answer: Often, yes. Finance for a sole trader, a partnership of two or three partners (not all of them companies) or another unincorporated body can still be regulated consumer credit, so introducing those customers to finance needs FCA credit broking permission. Finance for a limited company is outside these rules, and some business agreements over £25,000 are exempt, although introducing them can still be credit broking.

sections.title: Which business customers are covered
rows: Private individual
Yes.
Sole trader
Yes. A sole trader borrows as an individual.
Partnership of two or three partners, not all of them companies
Yes. The Consumer Credit Act includes these partnerships in “individual”.
Unincorporated body, such as a club or association, not made up entirely of companies
Yes. It is also included in “individual”.
Partnership of four or more partners, or one made up entirely of companies
No. It falls outside the definition.
Limited company
No. A company is neither an individual nor a relevant recipient of credit.

sources.label: legislation.gov.uk: Consumer Credit Act 1974 s.189 — definitions
legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 60L — relevant recipient of credit
legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 60B — regulated credit agreements

sections.title: The business-purpose exemptions
paragraphs: Credit over £25,000 is exempt where the agreement is entered into wholly or predominantly for the borrower’s business. Below that level, the business exemption applies only to green deal plans, so most van finance of £25,000 or less to a sole trader or small partnership remains regulated.

A business-purpose declaration by the borrower that complies with CONC App 1.4 creates a presumption, but it does not apply if the lender, or anyone acting for it, knows or has reasonable cause to suspect the agreement is not for business purposes. Hire agreements have a similar exemption where the hirer must pay more than £25,000 wholly or predominantly for business purposes.

sources.label: legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 60C — exempt credit agreements
FCA Handbook: PERG 2.7 — exempt agreements and business purposes
legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 60O — exempt consumer hire

sections.title: Exempt agreements can still involve credit broking
paragraphs: Credit broking includes introducing an individual or relevant recipient of credit to a lender for an agreement that would be regulated but for the business exemption. A dealer introducing a sole trader to exempt business finance over £25,000 is still carrying on credit broking.
Some CONC rules also apply to those introductions, including the commission disclosure rules in CONC 4.5.3R and 4.5.4R.

sources.label: legislation.gov.uk: Regulated Activities Order art. 36A — credit broking
FCA Handbook: CONC 4.5 — commissions

links: Read the credit broking permission guide

sections.title: Plan around your customer mix
paragraphs: Plan permissions around the regulated introductions you will make, not the vehicle type. A dealership selling vans to private buyers, sole traders and companies needs a process that identifies which rules apply to each customer.
bullets: Record the customer’s legal form before discussing finance.
For a partnership, count the partners and check whether any are companies.
Do not rely on a business-purpose declaration if you know or suspect the vehicle is mainly for personal use.

sources.label: FCA Handbook: PERG 2.7 — exempt agreements and business purposes
FCA: permissions and applications for motor dealers

sections.title: Fictional example: three van customers
paragraphs: Fictional example. Example Commercials Ltd sells used vans. A sole trader finances an £18,000 van for the business: the agreement is regulated, because below £25,000 the business exemption applies only to green deal plans.

A three-partner electrical firm finances £32,000 of vans wholly for the business and signs a compliant declaration: the agreement may be exempt, but the dealer’s introduction is still credit broking. A limited company’s finance is outside the consumer credit rules.

faqs.question: Do van dealers need FCA authorisation if they only sell to businesses?
faqs.answer: It depends on the businesses. Sole traders, partnerships of two or three partners (not all of them companies) and some unincorporated bodies are covered by consumer credit rules; limited companies are not.

faqs.question: Is van finance for business use always exempt?
faqs.answer: No. The business exemption covers credit over £25,000 used wholly or predominantly for business. Below £25,000, the business exemption applies only to green deal plans.

faqs.question: If the finance agreement is exempt, do we still need credit broking permission?
faqs.answer: Possibly. Introducing an individual or relevant recipient of credit to an agreement that would be regulated but for the business exemption is still credit broking.
